name: Posidonia oceanica meadows of Catalonia (Costa Brava)
description: Posidonia oceanica meadows of the Catalan coast, most of them on the Costa Brava: 10 agents, the meadow itself a keystone foundation species; the unit is the hectare and the reference resource is the regional stock (4,582 ha) unless the user enters the meadow a project affects. Every agent carries euros: the service ledger books each final ecosystem service once, to one agent (coastal protection, water purification, fisheries split between fish and invertebrates, bioindicator use split with the epiphytes, knowledge, recreational diving on the meadow and on the coralligenous, non-use values of megafauna and seabirds). Small losses are priced linearly (damage model area_loss). Carbon is valued by gaia.carbon. Sources: docs/POSIDONIA_LITERATURE_REVIEW.md; derivations: gaia/cases/definitions/CASE_NOTES.md.

resource.name: Posidonia oceanica meadows of Catalonia (Costa Brava)

area_ha.source: Generalitat de Catalunya, Mapa d'hàbitats marins de Catalunya (presented 29 May 2025; Hipermapa): P. oceanica meadows 4,582 ha, 2.4% of ~190,000 ha mapped to 50 m depth, as reported by Ara (29 May 2025, https://en.ara.cat/society/from-portbou-to-alcanar-this-is-the-catalan-seabed_1_5395705.html)
area_ha.note: The default reference resource: the whole Catalan stock (Portbou to Alcanar). A user assessing one project replaces it with the specific meadow the project affects (--area-ha N [--resource-name NAME], or resource.total_units/area_ha and resource.name in a copy of this file); the reference sets the depletion fraction, which matters once a project passes the safe threshold. The Costa Brava holds much of it (Cap de Creus) but the map's breakdown by coast was not available to this review, nor the dataset itself (the Govern's press-release PDF returned HTTP 403). The former 5,000 ha exceeded the whole Catalan stock.

unit_value.note: Project-specific input: the private gain per hectare of meadow destroyed (one-off), which the user sets with --unit-value for the project assessed. 2,500 is the former owner specification, kept as an illustration; no source can make it general.

safe_threshold_ratio.note: No ecological or regulatory source supports a 'safe' loss of 20% of a priority habitat (Habitats Directive 1120*): the value is the former owner specification. Under the case's area_loss damage model (Step 8c.3) it is the depletion of the reference resource beyond which the REMAINING meadow starts to degrade; below it each hectare lost costs exactly its average per-hectare value (linear benefit transfer). Monte Carlo range 0.1-0.3, uniform (judgement).

agent[*].dependency_weight.note: Owner-specified shares of ecosystem health (weights / 0.91 after the Blue Carbon agent was removed); no source. They set the health index and, with each agent's value, its € at full damage (weight × value = the sourced €/ha/yr service value).

edge[*].strength.note: Hand-set cascade strengths. The links themselves are documented (e.g. meadow -> wave attenuation: Infantes et al. 2012, MEPS 456:63-72, doi:10.3354/meps09754; seagrass -> fisheries: Jackson et al. 2015), their strengths are not. Monte Carlo range: ×0.5 to ×1.5 (judgement; wider ranges breach the in-degree cap).

steepness.note: Degradation of the remaining meadow past the safe threshold (damage model area_loss, Step 8c.3): zero up to the threshold, then a logistic with its inflection 15% into the post-threshold span (32% loss at the default threshold), the same curve for every agent. The damage of each agent is D + (1 - D) x degradation, so its slope at small losses is exactly 1 (each hectare lost costs its average value) and the curve shapes only the threshold behaviour. No Posidonia study relates the fraction of a meadow lost to the degradation of the rest, so the curve is not fitted (calibration regime B). Monte Carlo range 6-18, uniform (judgement).

agents.name: Posidonia Meadow
agents.description: The meadow itself, keystone foundation species; its own final service: the underwater amenity divers enjoy (recreational diving, Zunino et al. 2020)

annual_value_per_ha.source: Zunino, Melaku Canu, Marangon & Troiano (2020), Frontiers in Marine Science 6:823, doi:10.3389/fmars.2019.00823: choice experiment with 221 Italian scuba divers (2016-17); a total loss of P. oceanica cover lowers the willingness to pay for a dive by about EUR 34 (MNL, Table 3: -34.71); about 60,000 dives a year at the Medes Islands: Ràdio Capital de l'Empordà (26 May 2026, reporting the Parc Natural del Montgrí, les Illes Medes i el Baix Ter / SUBMON study: 'prop de 60.000 immersions anuals'); the former annual cap was 60,000 and the 2015 plan raised it to almost 77,000 (Ara, 19 June 2015)
annual_value_per_ha.note: Service ledger (Step 8c.2; docs/POSIDONIA_LITERATURE_REVIEW.md §2): recreational diving amenity of the meadow, 454.52 EUR/ha/yr = EUR 34.71 per dive x 60,000 Medes dives a year / 4,582 ha. Unit-value benefit transfer of a per-dive WTP from Italian to Catalan divers (no income adjustment); it assumes every Medes dive includes meadow (an upper-bias) and leaves out every other Catalan dive site (a lower-bias). Range 214-1,294 EUR/ha/yr: EUR 18.12/dive (the 50%-loss value, i.e. half the dives over meadow) x 54,000 dives to EUR 77/dive (latent class 1, total loss) x 77,000 dives (the plan's cap). Weight x value = the service.

keystone_threshold.note: Health below which the meadow's outgoing edges double; hand-set, no source. Monte Carlo range 0.15-0.45, uniform (judgement).

agents.name: Coralligenous & Red Coral
agents.description: Coralligenous reefs next to the meadow, smothered when it is lost (sedimentation); its own final service: recreational diving on coralligenous (Rodrigues et al. 2016, Medes Islands)

annual_value_per_ha.source: Rodrigues, van den Bergh, Loureiro, Nunes & Rossi (2016), Environmental and Resource Economics 63:289-311, doi:10.1007/s10640-015-9935-8: choice experiment with scuba divers at the Medes Islands MPA (Catalonia); the local extinction of gorgonians, the emblem of the coralligenous, costs divers about EUR 60 per dive; about 60,000 dives a year at the Medes Islands: Ràdio Capital de l'Empordà (26 May 2026, reporting the Parc Natural del Montgrí, les Illes Medes i el Baix Ter / SUBMON study: 'prop de 60.000 immersions anuals'); the former annual cap was 60,000 and the 2015 plan raised it to almost 77,000 (Ara, 19 June 2015); ~190,000 ha of seabed mapped to 50 m (Generalitat 2025 marine habitat map, as reported by Ara, 29 May 2025; see resource.area_ha)
annual_value_per_ha.note: Service ledger (Step 8c.2; docs/POSIDONIA_LITERATURE_REVIEW.md §2): recreational diving on the coralligenous, 18.95 EUR/ha/yr = EUR 60 per dive x 60,000 Medes dives a year / 190,000 ha of mapped seabed. A Catalan primary study; the attribution to a hectare of meadow is the seascape rule used for every service of the wider seascape: the regional value spread evenly over the mapped seabed (an assumption, not a source: no study links coralligenous condition to the nearby meadow). Range 9.5-43.8 EUR/ha/yr: half the attribution to EUR 108.01/dive (Zunino et al. 2020, total loss of coralligenous) x 77,000 dives.

agents.name: Epiphytes & Algae
agents.description: Epiphytic algae and plant community: primary production, food web base; owns the epiphyte share of the bioindicator service (PREI E/L metric)

annual_value_per_ha.source: Campagne et al. (2015), Marine Pollution Bulletin 97:391-400, doi:10.1016/j.marpolbul.2015.05.061, Table 2 (EUR 2014/ha/yr, French Mediterranean P. oceanica): use as bioindicator 1.5 EUR/ha/yr; share: Gobert et al. (2009), Marine Pollution Bulletin 58:1727-1733, doi:10.1016/j.marpolbul.2009.06.012, PREI EQR' = (N density + N leaf surface + N(E/L) + N lower limit)/3.5 with N(E/L) = [1 - E/L] x 0.5
annual_value_per_ha.note: Service ledger (Step 8c.2; docs/POSIDONIA_LITERATURE_REVIEW.md §2): an intermediate agent with no final service of its own: it owns the epiphyte share of the bioindicator service, moved from Human Communities (total unchanged): 1.5 x 0.5/3.5 = 0.2143 EUR/ha/yr, the weight of the epiphyte/leaf biomass metric in the PREI index used to monitor P. oceanica. Range x0.5-x2 (judgement).

agents.name: Marine Invertebrates
agents.description: Sponges, urchins, octopus, lobsters, shellfish: grazers and filter feeders; owns the invertebrate share of the commercial fisheries contribution (sea urchin, cuttlefish)

annual_value_per_ha.source: Campagne et al. (2015), Marine Pollution Bulletin 97:391-400, doi:10.1016/j.marpolbul.2015.05.061, Table 2 (EUR 2014/ha/yr, French Mediterranean P. oceanica): fishery contribution 27-35 EUR/ha/yr from 16 meadow-associated species sold at the Sète auction, two of them invertebrates (Paracentrotus lividus, Sepia officinalis), §3.2.4
annual_value_per_ha.note: Service ledger (Step 8c.2; docs/POSIDONIA_LITERATURE_REVIEW.md §2): the invertebrate share of the fisheries service, moved from Fish Populations (total unchanged): 35 x 2/16 = 4.375 EUR/ha/yr, by species count (2 of Campagne et al.'s 16 species; equal value per species is an assumption). Range 3.4-18.8 EUR/ha/yr: 27 x 2/16 to 74 x 0.254, the cephalopod and other-invertebrate share of Catalan white-fish, cephalopod and other-invertebrate first-sale value in 2014 (Generalitat, Estadístiques de pesca per grups biològics, dataset ge3m-4jgm: EUR 13.65 M + 0.34 M against 41.06 M; a proxy, not meadow-specific).

agents.name: Fish Populations
agents.description: Fish nursery and feeding habitat: contribution to commercial fisheries, fish species (Campagne et al. 2015)

annual_value_per_ha.source: Campagne et al. (2015), Marine Pollution Bulletin 97:391-400, doi:10.1016/j.marpolbul.2015.05.061, Table 2 (EUR 2014/ha/yr, French Mediterranean P. oceanica): fishery contribution 27-35 EUR/ha/yr (production function); upper end used
annual_value_per_ha.note: Service ledger (Step 8c.2; docs/POSIDONIA_LITERATURE_REVIEW.md §2): the fish share of the fisheries service, 35 x 14/16 = 30.625 EUR/ha/yr (14 of the 16 species are fish; the two invertebrates go to Marine Invertebrates). Range 23.6-64.8 EUR/ha/yr: (27 to 74) x 14/16. 74 is derived here, not published: Jackson et al. (2015, Conservation Biology 29:899-909, doi:10.1111/cobi.12436) attribute EUR 58-91 million/yr of Mediterranean commercial landings to seagrass; divided by the known P. oceanica area, 1,224,707 ha (Telesca et al. 2015, Scientific Reports 5:12505, doi:10.1038/srep12505), that is EUR 47-74/ha/yr (an overestimate per ha of P. oceanica).

agents.name: Marine Megafauna
agents.description: Dolphins, sea turtles: apex predators; their own final service: the non-use (existence) value of protecting charismatic marine megafauna (Börger et al. 2014, benefit transfer)

annual_value_per_ha.source: Börger, Hattam, Burdon, Atkins & Austen (2014), Ecological Economics 108:229-241, doi:10.1016/j.ecolecon.2014.10.006: choice experiment, UK households pay GBP 30.32/yr (mixed logit; 5-year tax) to protect porpoises, seals and seabirds on 50% of the UK Dogger Bank (GBP 24.02 on 25%); 2,989,357 households in Catalonia (Idescat, Households by size, 2021, from the INE Population and Housing Census); ~190,000 ha of seabed mapped to 50 m (Generalitat 2025 marine habitat map, as reported by Ara, 29 May 2025; see resource.area_ha); ECB euro reference rate, GBP per EUR, 2013 annual average 0.84926
annual_value_per_ha.note: Service ledger (Step 8c.2; docs/POSIDONIA_LITERATURE_REVIEW.md §2): non-use value of protecting marine mammals (dolphins) and, by extension, sea turtles, 30.18 EUR/ha/yr: the 5-year payment of GBP 30.32 annualised at the case's 2.3% (GBP 3.26/yr in perpetuity), converted at 0.84926 GBP/EUR (EUR 3.84), times 2,989,357 Catalan households (EUR 11.5 M/yr), spread over 190,000 ha of mapped seabed (the seascape rule) and split equally between Marine Megafauna and Seabirds, which Börger et al.'s attribute bundles. A unit-value benefit transfer from the UK (no income adjustment) of a protection scenario (50% of an area) read as the value at full damage: a lower bound in scope, an uncertain transfer. Range x0.33-x3 (judgement).

agents.name: Seabirds
agents.description: Seabirds that feed on meadow fish (Audouin's gull); their own final service: the non-use (existence) value of protecting seabirds (Börger et al. 2014, benefit transfer)

annual_value_per_ha.source: Börger, Hattam, Burdon, Atkins & Austen (2014), Ecological Economics 108:229-241, doi:10.1016/j.ecolecon.2014.10.006: choice experiment, UK households pay GBP 30.32/yr (mixed logit; 5-year tax) to protect porpoises, seals and seabirds on 50% of the UK Dogger Bank (GBP 24.02 on 25%); 2,989,357 households in Catalonia (Idescat, Households by size, 2021, from the INE Population and Housing Census); ~190,000 ha of seabed mapped to 50 m (Generalitat 2025 marine habitat map, as reported by Ara, 29 May 2025; see resource.area_ha); ECB euro reference rate, GBP per EUR, 2013 annual average 0.84926
annual_value_per_ha.note: Service ledger (Step 8c.2; docs/POSIDONIA_LITERATURE_REVIEW.md §2): non-use value of protecting seabirds (Audouin's gull, shags, shearwaters), 30.18 EUR/ha/yr: the 5-year payment of GBP 30.32 annualised at the case's 2.3% (GBP 3.26/yr in perpetuity), converted at 0.84926 GBP/EUR (EUR 3.84), times 2,989,357 Catalan households (EUR 11.5 M/yr), spread over 190,000 ha of mapped seabed (the seascape rule) and split equally between Marine Megafauna and Seabirds, which Börger et al.'s attribute bundles. A unit-value benefit transfer from the UK (no income adjustment) of a protection scenario (50% of an area) read as the value at full damage: a lower bound in scope, an uncertain transfer. Range x0.33-x3 (judgement).

agents.name: Coastal Protection
agents.description: Wave attenuation, beach-cast banquettes and matte stabilisation against coastal erosion (Campagne et al. 2015)

annual_value_per_ha.source: Campagne et al. (2015), Marine Pollution Bulletin 97:391-400, doi:10.1016/j.marpolbul.2015.05.061, Table 2 (EUR 2014/ha/yr, French Mediterranean P. oceanica): protection from coastal erosion 188 EUR/ha/yr (damage cost avoided, Mediterranean scale, 2001 data inflated to 2014)
annual_value_per_ha.note: 188 EUR/ha/yr of service at full damage = weight × value (service ledger, Step 8c.2) (188 / 0.142857). A single estimate; it covers wave attenuation, beach-cast banquettes and matte sediment stabilisation (Campagne et al.'s three services). Its spread in the Monte Carlo (×/÷2) is a judgement.

agents.name: Water Quality
agents.description: Nutrient and contaminant retention: the wastewater-treatment service (Campagne et al. 2015)

annual_value_per_ha.source: Campagne et al. (2015), Marine Pollution Bulletin 97:391-400, doi:10.1016/j.marpolbul.2015.05.061, Table 2 (EUR 2014/ha/yr, French Mediterranean P. oceanica): wastewater treatment 60 EUR/ha/yr (benefit transfer of the French water-protection tax, one third attributed to coastal systems after Costanza et al. 1997)
annual_value_per_ha.note: 60 EUR/ha/yr of service at full damage = weight × value (service ledger, Step 8c.2) (60 / 0.120879). A single, crude benefit-transfer estimate. Its spread in the Monte Carlo (×/÷2) is a judgement.

agents.name: Human Communities
agents.description: Cultural services: bioindicator use (leaf, shoot and lower-limit metrics) and knowledge (Campagne et al. 2015)

annual_value_per_ha.source: Campagne et al. (2015), Marine Pollution Bulletin 97:391-400, doi:10.1016/j.marpolbul.2015.05.061, Table 2 (EUR 2014/ha/yr, French Mediterranean P. oceanica): bioindicator use 1.5 + knowledge contribution 0.33 EUR/ha/yr; the epiphyte share of the bioindicator (0.5/3.5 of the PREI, Gobert et al. 2009, doi:10.1016/j.marpolbul.2009.06.012) moved to Epiphytes & Algae
annual_value_per_ha.note: Service ledger (Step 8c.2; docs/POSIDONIA_LITERATURE_REVIEW.md §2): bioindicator use without its epiphyte share (1.5 x 3/3.5) + knowledge contribution 0.33 = 1.6157 EUR/ha/yr. Beach tourism is still NOT valued (no Posidonia-specific welfare estimate); recreational-fisheries expenditure (EUR 112 million/yr for Mediterranean seagrass, Jackson et al. 2015) is spending, not welfare, and is not used. Its spread in the Monte Carlo (x/÷2) is a judgement.

stored_carbon_tonnes.source: Label Bas-Carbone, 'Méthode de protection des herbiers de posidonie' (French Ministry of Ecological Transition, approved 21 March 2023, NOR ENER2305073S; https://aida.ineris.fr/sites/aida/files/2023-04/Dec20230321_1.pdf), §7: the carbon in the living leaves is 'négligeable comparé au carbone stocké et séquestré dans la matte'
stored_carbon_tonnes.note: Living biomass is not counted separately: the leaves are negligible next to the matte, and the living rhizomes and roots lie inside the top-metre matte stock counted in soil_carbon_tonnes (counting them here too would double count). No Posidonia leaf-biomass carbon figure was verified for this review.

annual_absorption_tonnes.source: Mazarrasa et al. (2017), Limnology and Oceanography 62:1436-1450, doi:10.1002/lno.10510: organic carbon burial 26 ± 6 g C/m2/yr in Balearic P. oceanica meadows since 1900 (210Pb-dated cores) = 0.26 t C/ha/yr × 44/12
annual_absorption_tonnes.note: S5 resolved: one long-term burial (sequestration) rate, from the nearest region with direct measurements. Range 0.28-3.09 tCO2/ha/yr: 7.7-84.4 g C/m2/yr, the depth range of mean sequestration in a large Corsican meadow (Pergent-Martini et al. 2021, Marine Environmental Research 165:105236, doi:10.1016/j.marenvres.2020.105236). The former value, 1.58 tCO2/ha/yr, was the IPCC (2013) Wetlands Supplement Table 4.12 seagrass factor (0.434 t C/ha/yr, 95% CI 0.2-0.7, from Mateo & Romero 1997 and Serrano et al. 2012), which applies to revegetated meadows; it lies inside the range.

soil_carbon_tonnes.source: Monnier et al. (2022), Science of the Total Environment 838:155864, doi:10.1016/j.scitotenv.2022.155864 (39 matte cores, eastern Corsica: 327 ± 150 t Corg/ha), adopted as the Tier 1 default for 1 m of matte by Label Bas-Carbone, 'Méthode de protection des herbiers de posidonie' (French Ministry of Ecological Transition, approved 21 March 2023, NOR ENER2305073S; https://aida.ineris.fr/sites/aida/files/2023-04/Dec20230321_1.pdf); × 44/12
soil_carbon_tonnes.note: Organic carbon in the top metre of matte (the depth IPCC and the Label Bas-Carbone method treat as exposed), not the whole matte, which can be several metres thick. Range 741-1,844 tCO2/ha: 20.2-50.3 kg Corg/m2 in the first metre of matte in Calvi Bay (Leduc et al. 2023, Marine Environmental Research 183:105847, doi:10.1016/j.marenvres.2022.105847). Corsican, not Catalan, measurements; for scale, the IPCC (2013) global Tier 1 seagrass soil stock is 108 t C/ha to 1 m (Table 4.11) and Balearic P. oceanica holds 6.1 ± 1.4 kg C/m2 in the top 30 cm alone (Mazarrasa et al. 2017).

soil_release_fraction.source: Pendleton et al. (2012), PLoS ONE 7:e43542, doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0043542: 25-100% of near-surface (top-metre) carbon lost upon conversion, central estimate 63%
soil_release_fraction.note: A project input (--carbon-release-fraction): it depends on what the project does to the matte. Recommended values (docs/POSIDONIA_LITERATURE_REVIEW.md §4): excavated or dredged (port basins, channels) 0.96, the IPCC (2013) Wetlands Supplement Tier 1 for 'excavation to enable port, harbour and marina construction' (the top-metre soil carbon emitted in the year of extraction, minus 4% refractory); left exposed in place (meadow killed by shading, turbidity, anchoring or scour) 0.25-1.0, central 0.63 (this value, Pendleton et al.'s global range); buried under fill (breakwaters, reclaimed land) no source was found: the anoxic matte may keep much of its carbon (inferred, not sourced). The Label Bas-Carbone method models anchoring damage as a gradual loss (10.7% of the top-metre carbon over 10 years, after Mateo et al. 2019). The dominant uncertainty of the carbon externality.

release_half_life_years.source: Pendleton et al. (2012), PLoS ONE 7:e43542, doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0043542: at a converted site the rate of release 'likely follows a negative exponential curve with time', with 'a half-life on the order of 5-10 years' (their ref. 29, a cleared mangrove)
release_half_life_years.note: A project input (--carbon-release-half-life): the time profile of the release, valued year by year at the carbon price of that year and discounted. 10 years is the upper end of Pendleton et al.'s order of magnitude; seagrass evidence brackets it: the exposed share of Shark Bay's seagrass soil carbon was estimated released within three years of the 2010/11 die-off (Arias-Ortiz et al. 2018, Nature Climate Change 8:338-344, doi:10.1038/s41558-018-0096-y); soil stocks were 72% lower 50 years after a disturbance (Macreadie et al. 2015, Proc. R. Soc. B 282:20151537, doi:10.1098/rspb.2015.1537), i.e. a half-life of at most 27 years if the decay were exponential (inferred here); 4.8 of 6.4 kg Corg/m2 of the top 50 cm were lost under moorings deployed from the 1930s (Serrano et al. 2016, Sci. Rep. 6:23193, doi:10.1038/srep23193). Excavated matte: 0 (the IPCC emits it in the year of extraction). Range 0-27 years (judgement from these sources).

sediment_stability.note: No source: matte erosion after meadow loss depends on wave exposure (Salinas et al. 2020, Global Change Biology 26:4772-4784, doi:10.1111/gcb.15204, found soil carbon eroded in shallow exposed areas only). Affects only the restoration ceiling and substrate recovery time, not the extraction PV.

erosion_rate_unprotected.note: No source: matte erosion after meadow loss depends on wave exposure (Salinas et al. 2020, Global Change Biology 26:4772-4784, doi:10.1111/gcb.15204, found soil carbon eroded in shallow exposed areas only). Affects only the restoration ceiling and substrate recovery time, not the extraction PV.

erosion_rate_protected.note: No source: matte erosion after meadow loss depends on wave exposure (Salinas et al. 2020, Global Change Biology 26:4772-4784, doi:10.1111/gcb.15204, found soil carbon eroded in shallow exposed areas only). Affects only the restoration ceiling and substrate recovery time, not the extraction PV.

formation_rate.source: Serrano et al. (2016), Biogeosciences 13:4581-4594, doi:10.5194/bg-13-4581-2016: soil accumulation 1.2-2.0 mm/yr in meadows of the congener P. sinuosa (Australia)
formation_rate.note: A congener's soil accretion, rounded down; no P. oceanica matte accretion rate was verified for this review.

erosion_alpha.note: No source: matte erosion after meadow loss depends on wave exposure (Salinas et al. 2020, Global Change Biology 26:4772-4784, doi:10.1111/gcb.15204, found soil carbon eroded in shallow exposed areas only). Affects only the restoration ceiling and substrate recovery time, not the extraction PV.

rate.source: Drupp, Freeman, Groom & Nesje (2018), American Economic Journal: Economic Policy 10(4):109-134, doi:10.1257/pol.20160240: mean recommended social discount rate 2.27% (median 2.0%) from ~200 experts (Table 1 of the working-paper version, Grantham WP 172, 2015)
rate.note: The rate is the experts' mean recommendation, not a Ramsey sum: the survey's Ramsey components (median δ 0.5%, mean η 1.35, mean growth 1.70%) do not add up to it, and the former g = 1.3% had no source. A normative choice: the uncertainty analysis treats it as a sensitivity, not as a random parameter.
Step of the declining schedule (normative); no cited source for the value or the year.
Step of the declining schedule (normative); no cited source for the value or the year.

scarcity_rate.source: Drupp, Turk, Groom & Heckenhahn (2024), arXiv:2308.04400v3, §1: Dutch government default relative price change for ecosystem services
scarcity_rate.note: The Netherlands' default relative price change for all ecosystem services, as reported by Drupp et al. (2024, arXiv:2308.04400v3, §1; checked). Their own estimate is higher, 1.66%/yr for aggregate services (95% CI 1.40-1.92; regulating 1.71, cultural 1.91), but above the schedule's long-term 1.4% it would make the 200-year PV diverge, so 1% is kept. Normative: a sensitivity, not a random parameter.

horizon_years.note: A modelling choice; the outputs also report the PV at 50, 100 and 200 years (horizon sensitivity).

planting_cost_per_unit.note: An order of magnitude consistent with the all-habitat median, not a Posidonia cost survey. A Spanish planting guide (Red Eléctrica de España) cites US$383,672/ha for seagrass from the same paper; that figure was not checked against the paper. Transplant survival is low: 38% median for seagrass (Bayraktarov et al. 2016), 0-31% on disturbed substrate (Castejón-Silvo & Terrados 2021, doi:10.1016/j.marenvres.2021.105406).
planting_cost_per_unit.source: Bayraktarov et al. (2016), Ecological Applications 26:1055-1074, doi:10.1890/15-1077: median reported cost of marine coastal restoration ~US$80,000/ha (2010), real costs likely 2-4× higher, seagrass among the most expensive

steepness.note: Logistic recovery-efficiency curve of every agent (gaia.recovery default; inflection at 60% of lost units replanted).

pioneer_end_year.source: Kendrick, Marbà & Duarte (2005), Estuarine, Coastal and Shelf Science 65:717-725, doi:10.1016/j.ecss.2005.07.007 (agent-based model of P. oceanica colonisation): 'limited cover after a century of growth'
pioneer_end_year.note: Natural recolonisation from scattered patches; transplanting may be faster but its survival is low and long-term results are lacking (Pansini et al. 2022, doi:10.1016/j.scitotenv.2022.158320).

intermediate_end_year.source: Kendrick, Marbà & Duarte (2005), Estuarine, Coastal and Shelf Science 65:717-725, doi:10.1016/j.ecss.2005.07.007 (agent-based model of P. oceanica colonisation): growth accelerates after 100 years and plateaus after 400
intermediate_end_year.note: Model result, not a field time series.

pioneer_service.note: 'Limited cover' after 100 years (Kendrick et al. 2005) read as 10% of the mature service: an interpretation, not a number from the paper.

run.report_note:
⚠  MARINE EXTERNALITY NOTE: the per-agent costs are ANNUAL (€/yr) — they
     recur every year the meadow is gone. P. oceanica grows centimetres a year;
     natural recolonisation leaves limited cover after a century (Kendrick et
     al. 2005). Every agent's value is a final service booked once in the
     case's service ledger; beach tourism and the meadow's own non-use value
     are still not valued. Sources: docs/POSIDONIA_LITERATURE_REVIEW.md.
json_notes: Marine externality costs are ANNUAL (€/yr): they recur every year the meadow is gone. P. oceanica rhizomes grow only centimetres a year and a model of natural recolonisation leaves limited cover after a century (Kendrick et al. 2005), so loss is effectively permanent on human timescales. The net social cost compares the one-off private gain with the present value of these annual losses and of the carbon released. Every agent's euro value is a final ecosystem service booked once in the case's service ledger (Step 8c.2); beach tourism and the meadow's own non-use value are still not valued, so the services total remains a lower bound.
